version.changelog:
**Summary:** Improves environment variable handling, strictly separates local/cloud logic, and introduces new checks and documentation.

- Added `scripts/preflight_check.sh` to validate required defaults, skipping prompts when config is set via environment variables.
- Now strictly separates local (`scripts/collect_and_export_loop.sh`) and cloud (`scripts/cloud_dispatch_loop.sh`) send-command scripts—never mixes the two.
- Improved setup logic: never asks users for configuration if already present in environment variables.
- Bundled a new reference guide (`references/learning-guide.md`) for ambiguous or complex requests.
- Updated user flow and prompts to reflect the new logic and prevent redundant questions.
- Expanded documentation in SKILL.md to clarify setup, execution flow, and resource usage.

llm.summary: The skill's scripts and runtime instructions access cloud tokens, device IDs, and require curl/node and local bridge control, but the registry metadata does not declare these credentials or binaries — the mismatch and an undocumented cloud endpoint (https://i-sync.cn) warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a browser-extension collection helper. That purpose legitimately requires contacting a local bridge or a cloud dispatch endpoint and storing small preference files — but the package metadata declares no required environment variables or binaries while the scripts clearly expect WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_TOKEN, WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_DEVICE_ID, WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_URL, WEB_COLLECTION_CONNECTION_MODE and require curl and node. The missing declarations are an incoherence: a cloud dispatch flow needs a bearer token and device id, and the scripts accept/require them even though the registry shows none.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the helper scripts instruct the agent to run local shell scripts that: probe and call local HTTP endpoints (default http://127.0.0.1:19820), optionally start a user-supplied bridge command (this executes arbitrary shell via nohup bash -lc "$BRIDGE_CMD"), persist preferences under $HOME/.openclaw/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json, and (in cloud mode) send payloads and a bearer token to a fixed cloud base URL (default https://i-sync.cn). The instructions may therefore read/write local files and transmit user-provided API tokens and payloads to an external domain. The SKILL.md states some constraints (do not rewrite payload, do not call local 19820 from cloud path), but the scope includes file I/O and network exfiltration of collected data and tokens — all expected for the stated function but not documented in registry metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only with included scripts). That lowers install risk because nothing is downloaded at install time. However, the scripts will be executed at runtime and rely on external binaries (node, curl); the code is present in the bundle, not fetched from remote sources.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill bundle and SKILL.md rely on sensitive values (cloud bearer token and device id) and many environment variables (WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_TOKEN, WEB_COLLECTION_CLOUD_DEVICE_ID, WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_URL, WEB_COLLECTION_CONNECTION_MODE, WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD) but the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. Cloud mode will send Authorization: Bearer <token> to the default cloud base URL (https://i-sync.cn) — this is sensitive behavior that should have been declared. The scripts also read/write preference files under the user's home directory and may mask tokens when showing them, but they still persist tokens in preferences.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes persistent preference files to $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json (fallback $HOME/.openclaw/...), which is expected for preference storage. always is false. The script can also start a bridge command provided by the user (executes via nohup bash -lc), which can run arbitrary commands if the user supplies them; this is a user-controlled action but increases runtime privilege if misused. No evidence the skill modifies other skills or global agent config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will run shell scripts shipped with the skill that contact a local bridge (default http://127.0.0.1:19820), may start a bridge command you supply, persist preferences in $HOME/.openclaw/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json, and — in cloud mode — send your provided bearer token and payloads to a remote cloud endpoint (default https://i-sync.cn). The registry metadata did not declare the required binaries (node, curl) or the sensitive env vars (cloud token/device id) that the scripts use; treat that as a red flag. Before installing: (1) verify/trust the cloud endpoint (i-sync.cn) and the skill author; (2) prefer local mode if you don't want tokens sent externally; (3) avoid pasting secrets into chat — set tokens via environment variables only if you understand where they'll be sent; (4) inspect the scripts yourself or run them in a safe sandbox to confirm behavior; and (5) be cautious about using any --bridge-cmd value you don't fully control, since the scripts will execute it.
llm.findings: [no-static-findings] unexpected: The provided pre-scan reported no findings, but the included scripts contain network calls (curl) that send bearer tokens to a third-party domain and perform local filesystem writes and child-process execution; these behaviors are significant even if regex scanner did not flag them.
